title: A Border for the Debt
premise: Silas Pemberton, a war-weary interpreter for a faltering trilateral peace delegation, discovers that a diplomatic flight carrying evidence of a cross-border arms-for-hostages deal has been erased from every registry while still airborne — and that they were aboard it, which makes them either a witness or a loose end. Hunted by an assassin working for the consortium behind the deal, Silas smuggles the flight's true manifest and a dead negotiator's testimony through three hostile governments, learning that the conspiracy was funded by their own late father's inheritance and that their brother helped broker it. In the end Silas trades their own immunity and career to broadcast the truth at the signing ceremony, surviving the assassin but exiled from the profession and the country that shaped them.
about_author: Ivo Yarrow is the pen name of a former humanitarian translator who spent a decade in contested border regions before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose fluency in other people's words becomes the most dangerous skill they own.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. During a stalled peace summit, Silas interprets a negotiation that quietly collapses when one delegation's negotiator, Ansel Voss, slips them a sealed folder before boarding a return flight. Minutes later, the flight vanishes from every radar, log, and passenger list — including Silas's own name on it. The emotional beat is vertigo: a professional whose job is precision watching reality get rewritten around them.

chapters.title: Three Borders, One Bullet
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with a cold interlude in the assassin Meret's perspective. Fleeing across a land border with Voss's folder, Silas decodes the manifest: weapons moved under hostage-cover, signed off by a broker using their family's name. Meret closes in, killing a fixer who helped Silas. The beat is pursuit and dawning betrayal — the conspiracy has roots in Silas's own inheritance.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Cornered in a neutral city, Silas confronts their brother Tomas, who confesses he laundered their father's estate into the arms deal believing it would buy peace faster than diplomacy. Meret arrives; Tomas is fatally wounded passing Silas the final ledger access. The beat is grief weaponized into resolve — Silas stops running and chooses to carry the truth to the signing table.

chapters.title: Read Into the Record
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, closing with Meret's. At the summit's final signing, Silas uses their interpreter's credentials to hijack the simultaneous-translation channel, reading the ledger aloud in three languages while Meret hunts them through the hall. Security intervenes; Meret, ordered to make it look accidental, instead stands down and walks away. The deal collapses, the truth is on the record, and Silas surrenders their badge — free, and finished. The beat is costly, quiet justice.
